children: Meta Platforms, the social media and AI company

, approaches Wednesday's earnings report with a big question: how much cash will its AI push leave behind? Shares traded at $698.97, down 0.92%, at 8:05 a.m. ET on October 20 in premarket trading. According to Reuters, analysts expect revenue of $63.42 billion. That puts expectations just $580 million below management's $64 billion guidance ceiling. A solid sales number already has a high bar to clear.

The spending bill makes that bar more demanding. Meta's July results release put second-quarter operating cash flow at $31.86 billion and capital expenditure, including finance-lease principal payments, at $31.08 billion. That left just $784 million in free cash flow. In other words, capital spending swallowed roughly 97.6% of operating cash flow. Management also projected $130 billion$145 billion in full-year capital expenditure. The advertising engine is generating enormous cash, but the infrastructure buildout is consuming almost all of it.

The GF Score of 99/100 signals broad fundamental strength, with profitability, growth and GF Value standing out while momentum trails the other categories. That supports the business-quality case, but it cannot settle the cash-flow question. Revenue expectations sit only about 0.9% below the top of guidance, so a modest sales beat alone would say little about whether spending pressure is easing. Wednesday's sharper test is whether cash generation can pull further ahead of investmentand whether management's updated outlook gives investors reason to expect that gap to widen.

title: Meta Stocks Fall Ahead of Earnings With Just $580 Million Revenue Headroom
